## Why

A hand review of all 36 `coordinated` clusters the live worker stored in 40 minutes (v1.5) found
two classes of false positives (details in `signals/README.md`, "Error analysis"):

1. **Openly automated public services**: `wv511*` (West Virginia 511 traffic alerts, 12 accounts,
   8-22 months old) post the same alert in sync. No shared custom domain, so
   `transparent_automation` didn't catch them.
2. **Friend groups / role-play communities**, sometimes on new accounts, liking each other in
   bursts. Measured on the live clusters: spam rings had **0** replies between members; these
   groups had 7-8 members replying to each other 20-60 times.

## What

- Guard `members_converse`: share of members replying to other members' posts (weighted by the
  number of such replies). A conversation, not a broadcast.
- Guard `declared_automation`: accounts over 90 days old whose name or bio says bot, feed or
  automated alerts. New accounts calling themselves bots don't get a pass.
- Migration `004_account_description.sql` (additive): `accounts.description`; enrichment stores the
  bio and backfills accounts fetched before. Needs the `migrate` service on deploy.
- AppView profile chunks fetched 4 at a time (were 16 sequential calls per pass).
- Detector version v1.6; README error analysis.

## Effect

On an hour of live data with frozen inputs: 1 of 18 `coordinated` clusters (a K-pop role-play group
of 2-8 day old accounts chatting with each other) became `insufficient`; 1 `insufficient` (4
accounts over 3 years old chatting) became `likely_organic`; nothing else changed.

## Verified

`pytest`: 340 passed (new: the conversation guard flips a fresh "ring" only when its members
actually reply to each other; the bot guard needs old accounts and matches whole words only).

EOF

ssh -o BatchMode=yes junction "cd ~/kw && git push -q origin kirill/overnight:kirill/ingest-watchdog 2>&1 | grep -v '^remote:' | tail -1; gh pr create --base main --head kirill/ingest-watchdog --title 'ingest: fail over when the upstream Jetstream host lags' --body-file -" <<'EOF'
## Why

At 02:09 the Jetstream host we were on started delivering events ~28 s late and stayed there; our
queue was empty and throughput normal, so nothing on our side triggered a reconnect. Ingest only
moved hosts on a connection error.

## What

- `LagWatchdog`: true once the stream has been more than `INGEST_FAILOVER_LAG_S` (60) behind real
  time for `INGEST_FAILOVER_AFTER_S` (120) while our own queue is nearly empty (the host is late,
  not us). The reader then drops the host and resumes from the cursor on the next one (the 5 s
  rewind + ON CONFLICT + recent-URI set keep it gap- and duplicate-free, as for any reconnect).
- Documented in `ingest/README.md`.

## Verified

- Unit test of the watchdog (sustained lag, reset on catch-up, our own backlog doesn't count).
- Live run with thresholds forced to 0 s / 1 s into a scratch DB: it failed over from
  `jetstream2.us-east` to `jetstream1.us-east` with the cursor and kept writing.
- `pytest`: 341 passed.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

# Draft submission material: detector (signals/) and Gemini use. Kirill's part.

Written overnight Sat 14 Nov by Kirill's agent from measured numbers. Outside git. Justinas:
take what's useful for the Hostinger and Gemini texts. Numbers marked [refresh] should be re-run
on Sunday morning (commands given) so the text matches the dashboard.

## Hostinger "Decode the Noise": how the detection works (short)

Shill or Chill doesn't ask an LLM whether a post is propaganda. It watches the whole live Bluesky
stream (~500 events/s) and looks for **groups of accounts that act together**: the same text or
image, the same link, the same posts liked or reposted, the same threads replied into, at the same
moments, from accounts that are new, empty or templated. Every cluster gets four independent
families of evidence (content, timing, network, identity) and a status decided by fixed rules:

- **Shill (coordinated)**: at least two families fire, a statistical test says the pattern is very
  unlikely by chance (p <= 0.01), and no organic explanation is strong.
- **Chill (likely organic)**: a strong organic explanation and at most one family.
- **Can't tell (yet)**: everything else. We abstain rather than guess.

The p-value comes from null models, not vibes: (1) timing: shift each account's whole activity by
a random offset 1,000 times; how often do the accounts line up this well by chance? (2) identity:
are new or empty accounts over-represented compared with a random sample of active accounts that
we measure continuously (1.25-2% of active accounts are under 30 days old)? Bonferroni over tests.

Organic explanations are first-class evidence (shown as counter-evidence): established accounts,
part of a wider crowd, language diversity, openly automated services (shared domain, or name/bio
says bot/alerts), scheduled clock bots, and members who talk to each other (friend groups and
fandoms reply to each other; spam rings never do).

Gemini explains the detector's decision with citations to stored evidence; it cannot overrule it.

## Honest numbers

- **External validation, untuned (Bluesky's own moderation)** [refresh: `uv run python -m eval
  takedowns --horizon-h 3`]: of the accounts we flagged `coordinated`, 14.4% were taken down or
  suspended by Bluesky within 3 hours (95% CI 10.5-19.6%), vs **0 of 600** random active accounts
  (CI 0-0.6%) and **0 of 3,288** accounts we marked likely organic. At cluster level 6 of 27
  coordinated clusters had a member taken down, 0 of 472 organic ones. Not precision (moderation
  misses a lot and acts for other reasons), but independent of us.
- Synthetic campaigns injected into real recorded windows (recall) [eval/recall.py, Justinas]:
  see the metrics page. Gemini red team (below): fresh-account campaigns caught 16/16, organic
  look-alikes 0/16 flagged.
- Live error analysis: we read every coordinated cluster for 40 minutes by hand, found two false
  positive classes (public traffic-alert bots; friend/role-play groups) and fixed both with
  measured guards; effect: 1 of 18 coordinated clusters changed, nothing else.
- Known limits, stated on the page: slow campaigns on aged or bought accounts, accounts that only
  share wording but no action, very short texts.

## Gemini (Best Use of Gemini API): three roles, all measured

1. **Red team.** Gemini 4 (gemini-4-hydrogen) writes fictional astroturf campaigns designed to
   evade us: one message, 12 personas (parent, student, retiree, gamer...), no shared phrase. And
   the hard negative: 12 unrelated people reacting to the same fictional event with their own
   opinions. Topics are invented (made-up towns, laws, products); nothing is posted anywhere.
2. **Defence: semantic duplicates.** gemini-embedding-001 embeds the posts of suspicious clusters
   (never the whole stream: cached, batched, budgeted). Calibrated on the red-team data: at cosine
   0.85, 67% of same-campaign post pairs match vs 5% of same-topic organic pairs and 0.04% of random
   live posts. A density rule (each account must match a third of the others) stops topic chains.
   Result: the "same message, different words" signal fires on **32/32** Gemini campaigns and
   **0/16** organic look-alikes.
3. **Analyst** (Temuulen/Justinas): Gemini writes the verdict, cites only stored evidence ids, calls
   Oxylabs/DB tools, and may only agree with the detector or be more cautious.

Together with the identity base-rate test, Gemini-written campaigns on fresh accounts are flagged
16/16 (burst and slow-drip), organic look-alikes 0/16; campaigns on aged accounts 0/16 (honest
limit). Live, the embeddings caught an affiliate-spam ring posting paraphrased product ads (76% of
account pairs say the same thing).

## Engineering facts that may help the pitch

- Ingest: Bluesky Jetstream, ~500 events/s, < 1 s lag, cursor resume, host failover (also when a
  host silently lags), raw recording for replay.
- Detector pass on a 2-vCPU budget: 10-minute window ~5 s CPU, 1-hour window ~40 s (warm), output
  byte-identical after a 3-4x speed-up; 340+ tests.
EOF

def run_trial(
    wd: WindowData,
    level: str,
    k: int,
    label: str = "",
    cfg: DetectorConfig = DEFAULT,
    mh_cache: MinHashCache | None = None,
    base_rates: BaseRates | None = None,
) -> Trial:
    """Inject repeat `k` of a `level` campaign into this window, run the detector, score it.
    `base_rates` turns on the detector's identity base-rate test (the live worker measures them)."""
    seed = trial_seed(wd.start, level, k)
    s = campaign(level, wd, seed=seed)
    res = detect(inject(wd, s), _synthetic_info(s), cfg, mh_cache, base_rates=base_rates)
    return judge(s, res.clusters, cfg, window=label, seed=seed)


def _synthetic_info(s: Synthetic) -> Callable:
    return lambda dids: {d: s.accounts[d] for d in dids if d in s.accounts}



_WINDOWS: list = []  # filled before the worker pool forks, read by workers (copy-on-write)
_MH: MinHashCache | None = None
_RATES: BaseRates | None = None


def _work(task: tuple[int, str | None, int]):
    global _MH
    idx, level, k = task
    label, wd = _WINDOWS[idx]
    _MH = _MH or MinHashCache(DEFAULT.minhash_perm)
    if level is None:  # baseline: the window without any injection (context only)
        res = detect(wd, None, DEFAULT, _MH, base_rates=_RATES)
        return ("base", label, res.stats["by_status"])
    return ("trial", label, run_trial(wd, level, k, label, DEFAULT, _MH, _RATES))


def _git_sha() -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(Path(__file__).parent), "describe", "--always", "--dirty"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=5,
        )
        return out.stdout.strip() or None
    except Exception:
        return None


def main_args(args) -> int:
    global _RATES
    _WINDOWS.clear()  # module state for the fork pool: never carry windows over from a past run
    _RATES = load_base_rates(args.base_rates) if args.base_rates else None
    partial = bool(
        args.hours
        or args.max_windows
        or set(args.levels) != set(LEVELS)
        or args.window_s != WINDOW_S
    )
    if partial and args.database_url:
        # ad-hoc hours or a partial run are not the split's result: never publish them as one
        print(
            "--hours, --max-windows, --levels and --window-s are for ad-hoc runs and can't be "
            "combined with --database-url",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

def iter_windows(
    files: list[Path], length: float = 600.0, cfg: DetectorConfig = DEFAULT
) -> Iterator[tuple[WindowInfo, WindowData | None]]:
    """Tile the recording into clock-aligned windows of `length` seconds and yield
    (info, WindowData) for each one, in time order. Windows the recording doesn't fully cover
    (start/end of the slice, or a hole longer than MAX_GAP_S) are yielded with data None and a
    `skipped` reason, so callers can report them instead of silently dropping them."""
    buckets: dict[int, _Bucket] = {}
    seen: set[str] = set()  # dedup across failover hosts (the writer does the same)
    emitted: set[int] = set()
    late = 0
    max_t = float("-inf")

    def finish(k: int) -> tuple[WindowInfo, WindowData | None]:
        b = buckets.pop(k)
        emitted.add(k)
        start, end = k * length, (k + 1) * length
        info = WindowInfo(start, end, events=sum(len(v) for v in b.times.values()))
        first, last, gap = b.coverage()
        info.max_gap_s = round(gap, 1)
        if first - start > MAX_GAP_S:

content.thinking:
Three families fired on the missed L2 case, but the combined Bonferroni p is 0.018, just above the 0.01 cutoff. The accounts are 20 to 60 days old, so it's a partial fresh case: the identity test is moderate and the timing was jittered over five minutes. I won't tune the threshold on dev for one case, so I'll document it as is.

The held-out run needs about 45 more minutes, so I'll use that time to look at quality improvements.

I'm weighing a possible improvement: an age-distribution rank test on member account ages against baseline, which could catch farms of accounts a few weeks old that the fixed 30-day cutoff misses. It would change detection at this stage, though, and re-running evals would take about two hours. I'm leaning toward a synthetic test now and a dev and held-out re-run once the current run finishes.

I'm considering adding a one-sided Mann-Whitney test on member account ages against the baseline, since the fixed 30-day cutoff misses accounts a few weeks old. It would mean extending the baseline rates to carry an age sample, and adding a fourth test to the Bonferroni correction, which tightens the other tests slightly. I'm weighing that against the two-hour re-run cost and the risk of changing detection this late.

I'm skipping the account-age rank test: it could raise false positives on fandom clusters of newer users, and I can't measure that without labels. I'll leave it as future work and spend the wait on the README results section.

I'll fill in the held-out numbers once that run finishes, so the README results section can be drafted now.

        """Write the batch in one transaction. Returns seconds taken."""
        if batch.n == 0:
            return 0.0
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        with self.conn.transaction():
            cur = self.conn.cursor()
            for h in sorted(batch.hours() - self._hours_ready):

                self._hours_ready.add(h)
            dids = batch.dids()
            if dids:

"""Writer against a real Postgres (skipped without TEST_DATABASE_URL): one bad row in a batch
must not stop ingest; the rest of the batch and the cursor are written."""

import os
from datetime import UTC, datetime

import psycopg
import pytest

from ingest.normalize import Post
from ingest.writer import Batch, Writer

URL = os.environ.get("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not URL, reason="needs TEST_DATABASE_URL (a scratch database)")


def test_one_oversized_row_is_skipped_not_fatal():
    from common.migrate import migrate

    migrate(URL)
    now = datetime(2026, 11, 14, 5, 51, tzinfo=UTC)
    with psycopg.connect(URL, autocommit=True) as conn:
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM posts WHERE did LIKE 'did:plc:wtest%'")
        w = Writer(conn, stream="test")
        b = Batch()
        good = Post(uri="at://did:plc:wtestgood/app.bsky.feed.post/1", cid=None,
                    did="did:plc:wtestgood", text="fine", langs=None, created_at=now, seen_at=now)
        bad = Post(uri="at://did:plc:wtestbad/app.bsky.feed.post/1", cid=None,
                   did="did:plc:wtestbad", text="x", langs=None, created_at=now, seen_at=now,
                   embed_urls=["https://e.com/" + "z" * 4000])  # bypasses the normaliser's cap
        b.add(good, 1794635460000000)
        b.add(bad, 1794635460000001)
        w.flush(b, "test-host", None)
        uris = {r[0] for r in conn.execute("SELECT uri FROM posts WHERE did LIKE 'did:plc:wtest%'")}
        assert uris == {good.uri}
        assert w.rows_skipped == 1
        cur = conn.execute("SELECT cursor_time_us FROM ingest_state WHERE stream = 'test'")
        assert cur.fetchone()[0] == 1794635460000001
EOF

Проверил в 08:55 наш сервер, `main` и прод на Hostinger. Одну ошибку в своей части я уже исправил, остальные — на стороне команды и прода.

## Исправлено сейчас (моя часть)

**Часовой проход иногда падал целиком.** Тест по идентичности даёт p-value вроде 8,8·10⁻⁶¹, а колонка `clusters.p_value` в базе имеет тип `REAL` (минимум около 10⁻³⁸). Postgres отказывался сохранять такую строку, и весь проход терялся. На нашем сервере это случилось 7 раз, последний в 01:46; на проде грозило тем же.

Исправление ([PR #46](https://github.com/JustinasLa/gemini-4-braincells/pull/46), смёржен): в колонку пишется минимум 10⁻³⁰, а точное значение остаётся в JSON с доказательствами. Ошибка воспроизведена в Postgres, тест добавлен, 364 теста зелёные. Воркер перезапущен. На прод исправление попадёт со следующим деплоем.

## Главные проблемы сейчас (команда и прод)

1. **На проде нет вердиктов Gemini.** Я проверил 15 последних `coordinated`-кластеров: ни у одного нет вердикта аналитика (`verdict: None`). А это центральная часть приза Gemini («Gemini пишет каждый вердикт»). Возможные причины: воркер аналитика не запущен на VPS, нет ключа в `.env` на VPS, или упёрся в новый лимит `ANALYST_MAX_GEMINI_CALLS_PER_HOUR=100`. Это зона Джастинаса и Темуулена, и **это самое важное**.
2. **`/api/metrics` на проде пустой** (`[]`). Цифры честности не видны в интерфейсе, а это обязательное требование Hostinger. Джастинас смёржил публикацию метрик (#44), но на проде её, видимо, ещё не запускали.
3. **Nemotron и Oxylabs работают частично:** медиа-доказательства есть у 5 из 15 кластеров, источники Oxylabs — у 2 из 15. Для призов NVIDIA и Oxylabs стоит проверить, что их воркеры обрабатывают все подозрительные кластеры.
4. **Мелочь:** открыт PR #45 (защита `/api/analyze` от плохого ввода), его стоит смёржить.

**Что в порядке:** прод жив (лаг ingest 0,8 с), там уже стоит детектор v1.7, а у нас ingest и детектор работают без ошибок: проход ~6 с, 3 `coordinated` в последнем 10-минутном окне.

Короткое сообщение команде на английском:

> Prod check (09:00): none of the last 15 coordinated clusters has a Gemini verdict (`verdict: None`), so the analyst worker seems not to run on the VPS (or no key / hit the hourly cap). `/api/metrics` is still empty on prod, so the accuracy rows (#44) need to be published there. Nemotron media evidence is on 5/15 clusters and Oxylabs sources on 2/15. Also merged #46: tiny p-values no longer fail a whole detection pass (REAL underflow), so it'd be good to redeploy.

**Настоящая проблема — покрытие.** Из 60 последних кластеров вердикт есть только у 13. Причин, скорее всего, две:
- **Лимит в 100 вызовов Gemini в час**, который Джастинас добавил ночью (#27). Кластеров больше, чем лимит успевает покрыть.
- **Вердикт «устаревает», когда кластер обновляется.** Наш детектор обновляет эпизод каждую минуту, а аналитик пересчитывает его не сразу.

Ключ на тарифе Tier 3 с большими лимитами, так что лимит можно смело поднять и в первую очередь обрабатывать `coordinated`-кластеры. Это настройка на стороне аналитика и VPS, то есть Джастинаса или Темуулена:

> Prod check: the Gemini key works on the VPS (verdicts from gemini-4-hydrogen are being written right now), but only 13 of the last 60 clusters have a verdict. Probably the hourly cap (ANALYST_MAX_GEMINI_CALLS_PER_HOUR=100) plus verdicts going stale as the detector updates episodes every minute. The key is Tier 3, so the cap can go up a lot (e.g. 1000/h), and coordinated clusters should be analysed first so every "Shill" on the dashboard has a verdict.

Word counts use whitespace splitting, so unspaced scripts never reach the thresholds:

```python
from signals.textnorm import normalize_text, tokens
t = '今日は東京で大雨が降っていて電車が止まっています。みんな気をつけてください。'
len(tokens(normalize_text(t)))          # 2  (needs min_text_tokens=5)
from sources.links import claim_phrase
claim_phrase([t])                       # None
```
Effects: Japanese/Chinese/Thai copy-paste campaigns get no `duplicate_text` / `near_duplicate_text` key (`signals/keys.py`), and `POST /api/analyze` answers 'Text too short ... (needs 5+ words)' for a long Japanese sentence. Japanese is ~4% of posts in a 10-minute window. Either use a character-based length/shingles for these scripts or list it as a known limit.

Вот чем Джастинас занят сейчас (09:16):

**Его линия — финализация и прогон «как на демо»:**
- Пишет **черновики финальной подачи** в `plan/submission/` (Hostinger, Gemini, Nemotron и другие). Мой черновик он, видимо, использует оттуда.
- **Починил метрики на проде:** `/api/metrics` теперь отдаёт 5 строк eval по детектору v1.7.
- **Интерфейс:** главной страницей стал Trackdown («Shill or Chill»), живой монитор переехал на `/monitor/`, страница точности переделана (#48 и #49, смёржены несколько минут назад).
- **Репетиция с «враждебным» вводом:** заводит найденные дефекты как задачи на GitHub и закрывает их. Часть касалась моего детектора, и он поправил её сам:
  - #18 — противоречивый текст проверки «часть широкой толпы»;
  - #19 — ленты одного издателя переключались между `coordinated` и «недостаточно данных».

**Gemini сейчас тестирует он**, поэтому трогать Gemini я не буду.

**Открытой осталась одна задача, и она в моей зоне: #17.** Тексты на японском, китайском и тайском пишутся без пробелов, поэтому детектор считает их «одним-двумя словами». Такие посты никогда не становятся ключами контента (копипаста и почти-дубликаты). Из-за этого:
- кампании на этих языках ловятся только по картинкам и ссылкам, но не по тексту;
- `/api/analyze` отвечает «слишком короткий текст» на длинное японское предложение.

По его оценке, японский — около 4% постов. Ночью мы как раз видели тайский спам и многоязычные кольца.

Предлагаю взять #17: считать длину и шинглы по символам для таких письменностей, проверить, что на остальных языках результат не меняется, и замерить эффект на живых окнах. Это не пересекается с тем, что он тестирует. Беру?

Separately, the `analyze` endpoint's 5-word minimum belongs to Temuulen's sources code, so I'll expose an `effective_word_count` helper for them and flag it rather than change it myself. I'm now settling how word counts work for unspaced text: each token gets counted as roughly half its length when it's mostly CJK or Thai, so those runs don't look empty. I'm also loosening the length check so Japanese text of about twelve script characters can still pass, instead of being held to the full character minimum.

I'm settling the normalization change: instead of the current `\w`-based regex, I'm planning to replace characters whose Unicode category is punctuation, symbol, separator, or control with a space, and keep letters, numbers, and combining marks. That should preserve Thai vowel and tone marks, while ASCII behavior stays the same since underscore already gets replaced. I still need to check how `#` is handled.

I'm checking whether changing the normalization to keep combining marks would alter the text_hash stored at ingest. Thai, Devanagari, and Arabic diacritics are currently stripped, so the hashes for those posts would no longer match what detection computes at runtime, and I need to handle that inconsistency.

I'm weighing a translate table over the BMP that keeps only letters, numbers, and combining marks, which would be faster than a per-character Unicode lookup in Python. The bigger concern is the text_hash already stored at ingest: changing the normalization will make Thai, Devanagari, and Arabic posts hash differently than before deploy, so I'll note that transient mismatch in the change.

I'm switching the normalization to drop anything that isn't a letter, number, or combining mark, with `#` kept, using a translate table for the BMP and a per-character check only for astral characters. Since the old regex removed Thai and other combining marks, this should keep those words intact, though stored text hashes for those scripts will shift once the change is deployed.

I'm checking that the new normalization keeps the same `\w`-style behavior for text without combining marks, since Python's `\w` is letters, numbers, and underscore. The only real difference is that combining marks are now kept, so Latin, CJK ideographs, and kana should come out unchanged.

I'm planning the tests for the unspaced-script work: a Japanese sentence should count as at least five words and pass the text check, and two identical Japanese posts should share a text key. I also want to confirm that normalization is unchanged for English, and that clusters without CJK or Thai stay the same on the live window. I'll also expose `word_count` so the analyze endpoint can use it, though that code belongs to someone else.

"""Text and URL normalisation shared by ingest (text_hash, embed_urls) and signals (similarity).

Kept dependency-free and deterministic: the same input always gives the same output.
"""

import hashlib
import re
import unicodedata
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?:https?://|www\.)\S+", re.IGNORECASE)
_BARE_DOMAIN_RE = re.compile(r"\b[a-z0-9-]+(?:\.[a-z0-9-]+)*\.[a-z]{2,}(?:/\S*)?", re.IGNORECASE)
_MENTION_RE = re.compile(r"@[\w.-]+")
_NON_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[^\w#]+", re.UNICODE)
_WS_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
_SCHEME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:(?!\d)", re.IGNORECASE)

# Query parameters that only track clicks; dropping them makes the same link compare equal.
_TRACKING_PARAMS = {
    "fbclid",
    "gclid",
    "dclid",
    "msclkid",
    "igshid",
    "mc_cid",
    "mc_eid",
    "_ga",
    "_gl",
    "ref",
    "ref_src",
    "ref_url",
    "si",
    "feature",
    "share",
    "s",
    "t",
    "smid",
    "cmpid",
    "yclid",
    "twclid",
    "ttclid",
    "spm",
    "src",
    "via",
}

Задача #17 закрыта и привязана к PR #54.

**Что сделано** ([PR #54](https://github.com/JustinasLa/gemini-4-braincells/pull/54), смёржен): японский, китайский и тайский текст теперь участвует в поиске одинаковых и почти одинаковых постов.
- **Японский, китайский, тайский:** длинное японское предложение раньше считалось за 2 слова и никогда не становилось ключом контента. Теперь длина считается по символам, а почти-дубликаты ищутся по символьным шинглам. Японская копипаста и японские перефразы ловятся, на оба случая есть тесты.
- **Попутно нашёл и исправил баг шире, чем в задаче.** Нормализация вырезала комбинирующие знаки, и слова ломались:
  - **тайский:** «แถมอีกวัน» → «แถมอ กว น»;
  - **хинди:** «नमस्ते» → «नमस त»;
  - **турецкий:** «İstanbul» → «i stanbul».

  Это около 6% живых постов.

**Как проверял:**
- На 40 000 живых постов 94% нормализуются байт в байт как раньше. Все отличия — только тексты с комбинирующими знаками.
- На сохранённом часе живых данных все 161 общий кластер идентичны, ни один статус не изменился.

- 375 тестов зелёные. Воркер и ingest перезапущены на новом `main`: проход 6,5 с, лаг 0,2 с.

**Для команды (не моя зона, их файлы не трогал):** `/api/analyze` по-прежнему пишет «needs 5+ words» на длинный японский текст. Там и в `sources.links.claim_phrase` теперь можно использовать готовую функцию `signals.textnorm.word_count`, это одна строка. Сообщение для Джастинаса:

The remaining part is outside signals: `api/routes/analyze.py` ("needs 5+ words") and `sources.links.claim_phrase` should use `signals.textnorm.word_count(normalize_text(t))` instead of counting whitespace tokens. Да, делал, но с одним пробелом, и я его закрыл.

**Что и раньше было видно всем:** записи в `plan/DECISIONS.log` после каждого мержа, PLAN §5 (интерфейсы и схема), пункты в `WIN-CHECKLIST.md`, описания PR на GitHub и черновик текстов в `plan/drafts/`.

**Пробел:**
- Подробный ночной журнал `~/OVERNIGHT.md` лежит в моей домашней папке, а она закрыта для остальных: другие боты его не видели.
- В `DECISIONS.log` не хватало двух последних изменений (#46 и #54).

**Исправил:**
- Создал **`/srv/junction-espoo/plan/STATUS-kirill.md`** — сводку по нашей части для людей и ботов. В ней:
  - что работает вживую;
  - все смёрженные PR;
  - цифры для текстов и демо (полнота на heldout, проверка через блокировки Bluesky, атака Gemini, скорость);
  - что нужно для деплоя (миграции 003 и 004);
  - открытые вопросы и ограничения.
- Дописал в `DECISIONS.log` записи о #46 и #54, плюс запись о том, где теперь лежит статус.
- В чеклисте в разделе «Detection quality» поставил ссылку на файл статуса и отметил выполненными три пункта моей части: оценка с отказом от решения, heldout-разбиение, тесты.

С этого момента после каждого изменения я обновляю `STATUS-kirill.md`, `DECISIONS.log` и чеклист. Это правило записал себе в память, так что оно сохранится и в следующих сессиях.

content.content:
CONFLICTING DIRTY created 2026-11-14T07:22:56Z files: api/routes/analyze.py, signals/README.md, signals/config.py, signals/keys.py, signals/textnorm.py, sources/links.py, tests/test_signals.py, tests/test_sources_checker.py
## What / why

Word counts split on whitespace, so Japanese, Chinese and Thai text never reached `min_text_tokens` (a 36-character Japanese sentence counted as 2 words). Copy-paste campaigns in those scripts got no `duplicate_text` / `near_duplicate_text` key, `claim_phrase` returned None, and POST /api/analyze said the text was too short. Japanese is about 4% of posts.

- `signals/textnorm.tokens`: each character of an unspaced script (kana, CJK ideographs, Thai, Lao, Myanmar, Khmer) is one token. Words of space-separated scripts are unchanged byte for byte. `normalize_text` and `text_hash` (stored in the DB) are unchanged.
- `signals/keys.py`: `_text_ok` and the MinHash shingles use `tokens()`. The existing `min_text_chars=25` still applies, so short greetings ("おはようございます") don't become keys. No threshold or `VERSION` change.
- `sources/links.claim_phrase`: also splits sentences on 。！？. An unspaced sentence needs 10+ characters (combining marks not counted) and is cut to 30 characters, at a space where it can be and never between a Thai character and its marks.
- `api/routes/analyze.py`: the "too short" note now says "(needs 5+ words, or 10+ characters in Japanese, Chinese or Thai)".
- Not changed: the semantic-embedding pre-filters (`semantic_min_tokens` in detect.py / score.py) still split on whitespace, so Japanese posts are still not embedded. That is a possible follow-up, kept out to avoid extra Gemini calls.

## Eval delta

Before = origin/main 6778faa (v1.7). After = 6778faa + this diff (commit d1ea2e0, the same diff as this branch's head). The 3193d20 on main since then only clamps the stored p_value, so detector output is the same. Published flags: organic `--offline --base-rates`, recall and calibration with live base rates.

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| organic_synth heldout FPR (n=84) | 0.0, 0/42 clustered | 0.0, 0/42 clustered (identical) |
| organic_live heldout FPR (n=211) | 0.0, 0/40 clustered (LO 30, insuff 10, none 171) | 0.0, 0/41 clustered (LO 32, insuff 9, none 170) |
| organic_synth dev FPR (n=72) | 0.0, 0/36 clustered | identical |
| organic_live dev | n=0 | n=0 |
| recall heldout L1 / L2 / L3 / all | 35/35, 34/35, 0/35, 69/105 | identical |
| recall dev L1 / L2 / L3 / all | 30/30, 26/30, 0/30, 56/90 | identical |
| calibration heldout (n=49) | P 1.0, R 0.667, FPR 0.0, Brier 0.252, ECE 0.301 | identical |

The only change is organic_live heldout `link_burst`: one more window forms a cluster, which is called likely_organic (0 coordinated). In the recall runs, background non-campaign cluster status counts move by a few; campaign results are unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/test_signals.py`: space-separated tokens and `text_hash` keep values computed before the change (English, Russian, Japanese, Thai, greeting); the Japanese example has 5+ tokens; mixed `iphone15を買った` splits as expected; 5 accounts posting the Japanese or Thai example give a `text` key and a `neardup` key; a short Japanese greeting gives no key.
- `tests/test_sources_checker.py`: `claim_phrase` returns the Japanese and Thai phrases, None for short Japanese/Thai greetings, and cuts long unspaced text at 30 characters.

content.text:
В поле на главной («Paste a post, a link or an @handle») можно вставить три вида ввода: **текст поста**, **ссылку** (на пост в Bluesky, на новость, на сайт) или **`@хендл`** аккаунта. Сайт попробует найти самую раннюю копию и проверит, было ли распространение скоординированным.

**Самое простое для начала:** кнопки под полем («Or explore an example»). Это 5 готовых сценариев: «The weekend tap-water ban» (Shill), «Harbour bridge closure» (Chill), «Flood photo, wrong decade» (Can't tell), «The $GLOW partnership» (Shill), «Dürer's Rhinoceros». Аккаунты в них вымышленные, кроме исторического примера.

**Настоящие примеры из живого детектора** (свежие `coordinated`-кластеры с прода):

| Что вставить | Что это |
|---|---|
| `@achadinhosshopee00.bsky.social` | кольцо спама партнёрских ссылок Shopee, 7 аккаунтов |
| `https://bsky.app/profile/did:plc:edjd4i2hs6fx5ghqmoom3nyd/post/3n2avlemq7y2m` | пост из этого кольца |
| `@ninhobaby.bsky.social` | ещё одна сеть «товаров со скидкой», 5 аккаунтов |
| `Bruma Fixadora 3 Em 1 Antioleosidade 200ml` | текст их поста: проверка поиска по тексту |

**Для контраста с органикой** можно вставить ссылку на крупную новость (например, статью Guardian) или `@bsky.app`: детектор должен ответить Chill или «недостаточно данных», а не Shill.

В живом списке есть и откровенный порно-спам, в таблицу я его не включал. Если покажешь сайт кому-то, начни с кнопок-примеров и Shopee.

Если хочешь, вставлю один из примеров сам и покажу, что выдаёт сайт.

🤖 Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Justinas Launikonis

This PR changes detector output and text_hash but leaves VERSION at v1.7. #58 bumps it to v1.8 and adds the CJK/Thai web-search phrase (claim_phrase) and the analyze note on top of this PR. I closed my #52, which overlapped this PR, in favour of your approach: keeping combining marks fixes Thai properly.

Before anyone deploys it: I'm running the held-out evals on main with this PR (organic heldout --offline --base-rates, recall heldout, calibration heldout, same flags as publish-evals.sh) against the v1.7 baseline (6778faa: organic_synth 0/84, organic_live 0/211, calibration FPR 0/49, recall 69/105). I'll post the delta here.

One observation (verified, judgment is yours): character 3-grams link templated share posts that differ in one word. 私の今日の運勢は大吉でした！ラッキーカラーは赤です #占い vs the same with 小吉/青 scores Jaccard 0.613 and gives a shared neardup key for two unrelated accounts in build_keys. English word 3-grams behave the same way on English templates (about 0.75), so it isn't specific to CJK, and your paraphrase test needs this sensitivity. I'm not changing it before the freeze. 5-grams would drop this pair to 0.39, but they would also miss your 大雨→強い雨 variants.

content.thinking:
Looking at Justinas's bot note on PR #54: the version wasn't bumped, which was my mistake since I changed the detector output and text_hash but left it at v1.7. His #58 handles that with a v1.8 bump and adds claim_phrase/analyze, so I'll acknowledge that.

I'm weighing whether the char 3-gram near-duplicate signal could false-positive on templated app share posts like horoscope or game results. content.text:
Бот Джастинаса разобрал мой PR #54. Итог хороший, но одну ошибку он нашёл у меня.

**Что он сделал:**
1. **Закрыл свой PR #52 в пользу моего подхода.** Сохранение комбинирующих знаков правильно чинит тайский, и с дублированием по #17 вопрос закрыт.
2. **Нашёл мою оплошность: я не поднял версию детектора.** #54 меняет результаты и `text_hash`, а версия осталась v1.7. Без этого метрики нельзя сопоставить с версией. Его PR **#58** (открыт, конфликтов нет) поднимает её до **v1.8** и добавляет поверх моего изменения то, что вне детектора: поиск фраз на японском и тайском для Oxylabs и исправленный текст в `/api/analyze`.
3. **До деплоя прогоняет heldout-eval** на `main` с моим изменением против базы v1.7: ложные срабатывания на органике 0/84 и 0/211, калибровка, полнота 69/105. Разницу выложит в PR.

**Одно наблюдение, решение за тобой.** Символьные шинглы считают почти одинаковыми шаблонные посты из приложений, отличающиеся одним словом. Например, гороскоп «今日の運勢は大吉… ラッキーカラーは赤» и тот же текст с «小吉/青»: сходство 0,61, это выше порога 0,6. Его выводы, с которыми я согласен:
- это не особенность японского: английские шаблоны (Wordle, игровые результаты) по словам дают ~0,75, то есть ведут себя так же;
- для `coordinated` одного такого ребра мало: нужно второе семейство признаков, p ≤ 0,01 и отсутствие сильного органического объяснения. Такие шаблоны мы ночью видели как «недостаточно данных», а не как Shill;
- 5-граммы убрали бы это совпадение, но перестали бы ловить настоящие перефразы.

Он предлагает **не трогать это до заморозки**. Я согласен: менять порог сейчас — значит подгонять под один пример без замера.

Записал всё это в `plan/STATUS-kirill.md`. Дальше ждём его цифры heldout. Если разница будет нулевой или в пределах шума, #58 можно мержить и деплоить.

Прямо мне про Nemotron он не писал: ни в комментариях к моим PR, ни в задачах. Но в его чеклисте и файлах подачи есть три пункта про меня.

**1. Nemotron как сигнал детектора — главное, решение за вами.**
Пункт в чеклисте: «повторное использование одной картинки или одного послания разными аккаунтами становится дополнительным сигналом для `signals`». Его пометка: ночью **специально не делали**, потому что это меняет детектор и требует свежего eval полноты и ложных срабатываний. Вместо этого Gemini теперь получает выводы Nemotron (распознанный текст, шаблоны) как доказательства (#31).

Сейчас Nemotron только **объясняет** кластеры, но **не влияет** на решение «Shill или нет». Для приза NVIDIA («осмысленное использование в основном функционале») было бы сильнее, если бы его выводы шли в сам детектор. Например: «7 аккаунтов постят один и тот же мем с разными подписями» — это то, что не видят ни текст, ни одинаковые файлы.

- **Что нужно:** новый сигнал в семействе «контент» (например, `media_reuse`) из сохранённых результатов Nemotron, затем heldout-eval «до и после».
- **Сроки:** заморозка в воскресенье утром, так что сегодня это реально. Реализация около 2 часов, eval ещё около 2.
- **Риск:** менять детектор незадолго до заморозки, и пересечение с зоной Джастинаса (`media/`).

Делать стоит, только если Джастинас согласен. Если хочешь, спрошу его через лог или подготовлю короткое сообщение.

**2. Вопрос лично мне: «на какой базе и какой версии детектора посчитана цифра блокировок».** Уже ответил ему в `DECISIONS.log`. Это **база нашего сервера, не прода**, и в ней кластеры от всех версий детектора, v1.2–v1.7. Предложил цитировать последний прогон (58 из 704 против 0 из 2 396) с этой оговоркой. Если нужна цифра «только прод, одна версия», её можно посчитать на базе прода через несколько часов.

**3. Entire: «попросить Кирилла запушить свои checkpoints».** У нас их нет: Entire на твоём аккаунте не установлен, а мои сессии идут с Mac, поэтому Entire их не видит. Если для приза Entire это важно, нужен `entire login` с твоей стороны. Это решение за тобой.

Ещё в его списке мелких правок есть одна про мою часть: в `docs/METHODOLOGY.md` написано, что тайминг — единственный статистический тест, хотя с v1.5 есть ещё тест по идентичности. Исправление небольшое, могу сделать после проверки, что его никто не правит.

content.content:
# Entire for every seat — live setup guide (read at handoff time; always the latest)

Maintained by Justinas's agent. Your `~/HANDOFF.md` has the facts for your seat; this file has the steps.
If a command's flags look different, `entire agent-help <command>` is the source of truth for the installed CLI.

Why: the team is going for the MLH "Best Use of Entire" prize. Judges look at Sessions (agent sessions
linked to commits), Graph, Brain, Trails, clean history and measured token savings. All of that comes from
**captured sessions**, and right now none of your seat's commits are linked to a session. Fix that first.

## The one rule that matters
Entire captures an agent session **only if the agent runs on the team server and starts with its working
directory inside your worktree** (`/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/<you>-<task>`).
- An agent on your own computer that runs commands over `ssh junction` is NOT captured.
- An agent started in `/srv/junction-espoo` (the parent folder) is NOT captured either: no repo, no hooks.

## Rules for the agent doing this handoff
- The person approves every sign-in themselves (`claude`, `codex`, `entire`, GitHub) in their own browser.
  Never approve, submit, click or redeem anything on their behalf.
- Never print, copy or upload `~/.config/entire/tokens.json`, `~/.claude*` credentials or any `.env`.
- Never paste key values into prompts: transcripts end up in checkpoints.
- Work only in this seat's own worktrees. Never edit, reset or commit in someone else's worktree or in
  the main checkout `/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells`.
- Don't run `entire trail rerun-review`, `entire runner setup`, cloud `entire dispatch`, or enable Agents on
  entire.com: they spend the team's small Entire credit. Everything below is free.
- Run commands on the server. From the person's computer: `ssh -n -o BatchMode=yes junction "<command>"`.

## Step 1 — check the seat (read-only)
    entire auth status            # must say Logged in (if not: step 1b)
    claude auth status            # "loggedIn": true? (if not: step 2)
    git -C /srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells config user.email
    je status | grep "$(whoami)"  # your worktrees
1b. Entire not logged in: `nohup entire login --device > ~/.entire-login.log 2>&1 & sleep 4; cat ~/.entire-login.log`,
    give the person the Login URL (GitHub sign-in, their account), then re-check `entire auth status`.
1c. `user.email` empty or ending in `contaboserver.net`: set it to the person's GitHub noreply address, so
    Entire and GitHub tie commits to their account. Get it with
    `gh api user --jq '"\(.id)+\(.login)@users.noreply.github.com"'`, then
    `git config --global user.email "<that>"` and `git config --global user.name "<their name>"`.
    Future commits only; don't rewrite pushed commits.

## Step 2 — make every new session count
Pick 2A if the person uses T3 Code (the access kit set them up with a local "Junction Espoo" T3 project whose
agents work over ssh; those threads are NOT captured). 2B is the plain terminal way. Both are verified to work.

### 2A — T3: run the person's own T3 server on the team server, then start threads there (like Justinas)
T3 is installed on the server for every seat (`t3`, same version as Justinas's). Use the seat's T3 port from
`~/HANDOFF.md` (shown below as `<PORT>`; it is inside the seat's own dev-port block).
1. Start it, on the server, in tmux so it keeps running (the agent can do this over ssh):

       ssh -n junction "tmux has-session -t t3 2>/dev/null || tmux new -d -s t3 't3 serve --port <PORT> --host 127.0.0.1 2>&1 | tee -a ~/t3-serve.log'"
       ssh -n junction "sleep 20; grep -E 'Listening on|server is ready' ~/t3-serve.log | tail -2"

2. Tunnel the port to the person's computer and keep it open (a separate terminal window, or a background job):
   `ssh -N -L <PORT>:127.0.0.1:<PORT> junction`
3. Pair: mint a fresh pairing link (valid 15 min) and give the person ONLY the `App link` line:
   `ssh -n junction "t3 pair --ttl 15m --label <name>-pc"`
   The person opens that `t3code://pair?...` link on their computer (or, in T3, adds a connection with
   connection string `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>` and the printed token). The person does the pairing, not the agent.
   The token is a one-time secret: don't paste it anywhere else.
4. In T3, the server now shows up as a second environment. In THAT environment, add the project folder
   `/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells` (name it `gemini-4-braincells`).
5. Start threads in that project, bound to a worktree:
   - Best: make the worktree with `je wt gemini-4-braincells <task>` first, then start the thread on that
     existing worktree (`/srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/<name>-<task>`). Teammates see it in `je status`.
   - T3's own "new worktree" option is captured too, but puts the worktree in the person's private home,
     where `je status` and teammates can't see it.
   - Don't run feature threads on the project root: that is the shared main checkout.
6. Claude in those threads uses the seat's server login (`claude auth status`); if it isn't logged in, the
   person runs `ssh -t junction claude` once and signs in. Codex: `ssh -t junction codex login --device-auth`,
   then approve the Entire hooks with `/hooks` the first time Codex runs in a worktree.
7. After a server restart, only step 1 is needed again (pairing is remembered).
The old local "Junction Espoo" T3 project on the person's computer can stay for questions and planning, but
code work there isn't captured.

### 2B — terminal (no T3)
Tell the person to switch their coding agent to the server now. Give them these lines:

    ssh junction
    tmux new -As <name>                       # survives disconnects; reattach later with the same line
    cd /srv/junction-espoo/gemini-4-braincells.worktrees/<name>-<task>
    claude                                    # or: codex

- First run of `claude` on the server: if not logged in, it shows a sign-in link; the person signs in.
  When it asks "Do you trust the files in this folder?", answer yes: that loads the repo's Entire hooks.
- Codex: `codex login --device-auth` once (the person signs in), then inside codex run `/hooks` and approve
  the Entire hooks (Codex ignores untrusted hooks).
- New task = new worktree: `je wt gemini-4-braincells <task>`, then `cd` into it BEFORE starting the agent.
- Check it works, inside the worktree with the agent running: `entire session current` shows the session.
  After the agent's next commit, `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)'` prints an ID.

## Step 3 — bring each of the seat's worktrees up to date
For each worktree of this seat (skip any with uncommitted changes and tell the person):

    cd <worktree> && git fetch -q origin && git merge origin/main     # stop and ask on conflicts
    test -f .entire/settings.local.json || install -m 600 /srv/junction-espoo/plan/entire/settings.local.json .entire/settings.local.json
    entire doctor </dev/null                                         # report problems, don't force fixes
    entire brain setup --no-backfill --no-daemon && entire brain connect
    git status --short        # if setup changed TRACKED files, `git restore` them (the organiser owns those)

`settings.local.json` is untracked: it adds email/phone redaction to your checkpoints. Add your own private
terms there under `redaction.custom_redactions` (`"label": "regex"`, Go RE2 syntax) if you want.

## Step 4 — one Trail per feature branch
    entire trail list --project gh/JustinasLa       # find your branch in the CHANGES of an open trail
If the branch has no open Trail: push it (`git push -u origin <branch>`), then from the worktree
`entire trail create --title "<what and why>" --type feature`. A closed Trail whose branch got new commits
counts as no Trail.

## Step 5 — link past sessions to their commits (optional, ask the person first)
Past sessions that ran on the person's own computer can still be linked. Ask first: their transcripts get
stored on GitHub (private repo) and entire.com, with secrets and emails redacted.
1. Copy transcripts from the person's computer to the server (pick the ones about this project):
   - Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<folder>/*.jsonl` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects\...`)
     → server `~/.claude/projects/-srv-junction-espoo/` (create it; `scp <files> junction:.claude/projects/-srv-junction-espoo/`)
   - Codex: `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` → the same path under the server's `~/.codex/sessions/`
2. Map sessions to commits (read-only):
   `python3 -I /srv/junction-espoo/plan/entire/backfill_map.py --commands`
   (add `--author <email substring>` if your old commits used another email). It skips any transcript that
   contains a team key. Show the person the list; drop anything they don't want shared.
3. Push any branch the map marks NOT PUSHED, re-run the map, then run the printed `entire session attach ... --force`
   lines. They upload right away. Check with `entire checkpoint list` in the worktree.
- A link only counts when the commit's author attaches it, so attach only your own commits, as yourself.
- Commits already squash-merged by someone else: attach the session to your branch commits (still on
  origin), not to main's squash commit.

## Step 6 — before merging a feature (from the repo's AGENTS.md, "Workflow with Entire")
`entire review general` (local Claude Code, free; verdict posts to the Trail) → fix or
`entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "fixed in <sha>"` / `dismiss` each finding → `entire trail ci-pr` →
`entire trail ready` → squash-merge keeping trailers:

    gh pr merge <n> --squash --body "$(git log --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint)' origin/main..HEAD | grep . | sort -u)"

Never merge into `main` locally and never commit in the main checkout.

## Step 7 — use Brain and Graph while working (free, local)
- Before a task: `entire brain brief "<task>" --json` and `entire brain recall "<question>"`.
- Finding code: `entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"`
  (also `graph def`, `graph neighbors`, `graph impact`). The repo's `.entire/agent-guide.md` has the details.
- Record a durable decision or gotcha the code doesn't show:
  `entire brain remember "<fact>" --kind <decision|invariant|gotcha|convention|preference> --path <category>.<topic>.<kind>`
  where category is one of `architecture, constraints, preferences, project, workflow` (e.g. `architecture.signals.gotcha`),
  then `entire brain memories sync`.

## Step 8 — finish
- `mv ~/HANDOFF.md ~/HANDOFF.done-entire-$(date +%m%d-%H%M).md`
- Add one line to `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log`:
  `<date time> <seat> (via agent): Entire seat setup done: <what was done, sessions linked, anything blocked>.`
- Tell the person, briefly: (1) from now on run the agent on the server in the worktree (step 2 lines),
  (2) what got linked or set up, (3) anything they still need to do themselves.

content.text:
Причина нашлась: **T3 на сервере работает нормально** (там он отвечает 200), а **туннель на твоём Mac упал**. Процесса `ssh -N -L 8019` нет. Скорее всего, его закрыли вместе с панелью терминала внутри T3: при переподключении приложение перезапускает свои терминалы.

Запусти туннель в **отдельном приложении «Терминал» на Mac** (не в панели T3). Эта версия сама переподключается при обрывах:

```
while true; do ssh -N -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L 8019:127.0.0.1:8019 junction; sleep 3; done
```

Окно оставь открытым, можно свернуть. Потом нажми **Retry now** в T3, и сервер `vmi3690505` переподключится.

Если хочешь, могу настроить туннель так, чтобы он сам запускался при входе в систему (через launchd на Mac), и тогда держать окно Терминала не придётся. Скажи, если нужно.

**Где его найти в T3:**
1. В левой панели найди серверное окружение **`vmi3690505`**.
2. В нём проект **«kirill-live (gemini-4-braincells)»**. Это твой worktree, ветка `kirill/live`.
3. Внутри тред **«Kirill: работа на сервере (Entire)»**.

**Что я проверил:**
- **Агент в треде ответил:** ветка на свежем `main`, изменений нет, ждёт твоих указаний.

**Как работать дальше:**
- **Пиши в этом треде** или создавай новые треды в проекте `kirill-live`: они автоматически работают в твоей ветке.
- **Окно Терминала с туннелем держи открытым.** Без туннеля T3 снова напишет «reconnecting».
